title: FIRST PROPERTY TAX PAYMENT DUE
full_story:
The first installment of the 2025 payable 2026 Real Estate Tax Bill is due on Friday.  The Treasurer’s Office will be closed today in observance of Columbus Day.  If you have questions about your tax bill, please feel free to call the Treasurer’s office.  If you cannot get through, please leave a message, and they will return your call as soon as possible.  Phone 618-665-3727.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.

At the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money order.  Bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00-4:00 Monday through Friday, but closed on national holidays.

Online by credit/debit card: Go to www.govpaynow.com PLC #a00082.

Or by drop box at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

title: STATE POLICE CARS HIT
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) experienced two Move Over Law-related crashes during the past three days on Illinois interstates.

On Thursday, at approximately 11:49 pm, an ISP Trooper was stationary in a construction zone on Interstate 55 northbound near milepost 106.5, with emergency lights activated.  A black Mazda traveling northbound on I-55 struck the ISP squad car.  The Trooper was inside of the squad car at the time of the crash and was transported to the hospital by another Trooper as a precaution.  The driver of the Mazda, 43-year-old Tiffany Sipes of Williamsville, IL, was issued citations for Scott’s Law and Driving Under the Influence.

On Friday, at approximately 5:02 pm, an ISP Trooper was stationary on Interstate 70 westbound near milepost 85.5, with emergency lights activated and working an active crash scene.  A black Land Rover traveling westbound on I-70 sideswiped the Trooper’s squad car and struck another vehicle in the backed-up traffic.  The Trooper was outside the squad car and no injuries were reported.  The driver of the Land Rover, Amanda S. Thomas, 45, of Logan, IL, was issued citations for Scott’s Law, Improper Lane Usage, Leaving the Scene of a Property Damage Accident, Driving Under the Influence, and multiple other traffic offenses.

So far in 2026, ISP has suffered 11 Move Over Law-related crashes, resulting in two injured Troopers.  In 2025, ISP reported 15 Move Over Law-related crashes with seven Troopers injured.  In 2024, ISP had 27 Move Over Law-related crashes with 12 injuries and one death.  ISP reminds the public that the Move Over Law, also known as “Scott’s Law” in Illinois, requires all drivers to slow down and move over when approaching an emergency vehicle, emergency worker, or any vehicle with its emergency or hazard lights activated.

A person who violates the Move Over Law faces a fine of no less than $250 and no more than $10,000 for a first offense.  If the violation results in injury to another person, the violator’s driver’s license will be revoked.

title: CCH LAB FAIR
full_story:

The blood draws must be completed Thursday, October 15th through October 31st.  The hours for the blood draws are Monday through Friday, from 7 am till 7 pm and Saturdays from 7 am till 11 am at the Clay County Hospital.  Please complete your voucher before registering.  Payment is due at registration.

Regular blood tests are an essential part of your preventative health care plan.  Multiple choices of labs are available for you to select on the voucher.  The popular “Lab Fair Panel” results include the kidney and liver functions, complete blood count, and measure cholesterol levels and triglycerides.  Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics thanks you for choosing them as your choice of healthcare and they look forward to serving you during the “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” October 15th through October 31st.

title: TRUCK PARKING GRANT
full_story:
US Representative Mike Bost announced that he secured a grant from the US Department of Transportation to improve truck parking availability and safety along Interstate 57 in Effingham and Marion counties.

“Having grown up in the trucking business, I know firsthand how important it is for our truck drivers to have safe, reliable places to pull over and rest,” said Bost.  “These hardworking men and women spend countless hours on the road delivering the goods our families and businesses depend on.  The last thing they should have to worry about is finding a safe place to park.  That’s why I’ve made expanding truck parking a priority, and I’m proud to secure this funding to improve safety, strengthen our transportation infrastructure, and keep Southern Illinois moving forward.”

This announcement comes after Bost sent a letter of support to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy to emphasize the urgency of these improvements.  The $12.6 million investment will support reconstruction and expansion of the Green Creek South-Bound and Post Oak South-Bound rest areas, including the construction of new facilities, utility and drainage improvements, and the addition of approximately 38 truck parking spaces.  Additionally, the project will deploy Truck Parking Information Management System, including automated vehicle detection, electronic kiosks, and security equipment.

Interstate 57 is a critical transportation corridor for Southern Illinois, connecting local businesses, farmers, and manufacturers to markets across the country.  These improvements will address truck parking shortages while bolstering the safe and efficient movement of freight across the region.

title: TROUT FISHING OPENS
full_story:
The 2026 Illinois fall trout fishing season will open on Saturday, at 60 ponds, lakes and streams throughout the state.

An early catch-and-release trout fishing is now open at select sites.  No trout may be kept during the catch-and-release period.  Anglers may begin keeping trout when the regular season opens at 5 am Saturday.

In our area trout fishing can be done at Sam Dale Conservation Area Turkey Run Pond in Wayne County.  At the Boston Pond, in the Stephen A. Forbes State Recreation Area in Marion County, and at the Mount Vernon City Park Pond in Jefferson County.

The Illinois Catchable Trout Program is funded through the sale of inland trout stamps.  The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) stocks more than 80,000 rainbow trout each year at waters where trout fishing is permitted during the fall season.  An additional 80,000 trout are stocked for the spring season, which begins in April.

For the 2026 fall trout season, no trout may be taken from any stocked site before the season opens.  During the season, the daily catch limit is five trout.  All anglers must have a valid Illinois fishing license and inland trout stamp.  Check the IDNR agent locator website for locations. Fishing licenses and trout stamps are also available online.

Anglers should contact individual trout-stocked sites for information about site-specific regulations and opening times.  Not all sites open at 5 am on opening day.  Anglers are encouraged to check the opening time for their preferred fishing location before October 17th.

The fall trout season offers opportunities for families to get outdoors and enjoy fishing.  Resources are available for taking kids fishing online.  For more information on trout seasons and other Illinois fishing opportunities, visit www.ifishillinois.org.

title: OPEN ENROLLMENT OPENS SOON
full_story:
Before Medicare’s Open Enrollment period begins on October 15th, the Illinois Department on Aging (IDoA) is encouraging beneficiaries to start browsing plans early and to get trusted advice through the state’s Senior Health Insurance Program (SHIP).

“I want to express to people with Medicare Part D plans and or Medicare Advantage plans that it is necessary to check your current plan and the benefits offered for 2027.  Some premiums (for Part D plans) have gone from $0 per month to $6–$23 per month,” said SHIP Director Sandy Leith.  “It is good practice to make sure your prescriptions will still be on the formulary for next year’s plan or just shop around for a better Part D plan that may save you money next year.  If you take your Medicare through a Medicare Advantage plan, check to see what the copays for health and drug benefits will cost you in 2027.  There are some plans that are not renewing for 2027; make sure to contact your plan if you received a letter of non-renewal.  There may be other options within the same company for you.”

Medicare’s annual Open Enrollment Period, October 15th through December 7th is an opportunity for beneficiaries to join, switch, or drop certain Medicare plans.  Current beneficiaries should soon be receiving their plan’s Annual Notice of Change (ANOC), which summarizes the changes in their plan’s cost and coverage for the coming year.

An updated “Medicare & You” handbook was mailed to all Medicare households in late September.  The handbook is also available online in many different formats and languages, including large print, braille, and more.  It contains important information about, Medicare benefits, costs, rights, and protections, health and drug plans, and answers to common questions.

For additional help understanding Medicare options and how to save money, beneficiaries can contact Illinois’ Senior Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) by calling 1-800-252-8966 or emailing [email protected]. SHIP utilizes over 1,000 trained volunteers statewide who offer trusted, unbiased Medicare counseling.

Many SHIP sites are currently taking appointments to help beneficiaries navigate the decision-making process.  To schedule an appointment, contact a local SHIP site directly.  To make most of a counseling session, beneficiaries are encouraged to bring a list of their current medications and preferred pharmacies, along with any recent information received from your current drug/health plan.

title: DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME ENDS
full_story:
Millions of Americans will turn back their clocks Saturday night, October 31st, before going to bed, marking the end of Daylight-Saving Time in 2026.

The controversial practice of “springing forward” and “falling back” has been observed in most states for decades.  Under the current Daylight-Saving Time period, most Americans lose an hour of sleep on the second Sunday of March and gain an hour the first Sunday of November.

Daylight Saving Time ends Sunday, November 1st at 2 am.  We will “fall back,” turning our clocks back to 1 am, gaining an extra hour of sleep.

As the clock turns back an hour on that weekend, it’s also a good time to check your smoke detectors and make sure you have a fire escape plan that allows all family members to get out in two minutes if a fire occurs.

In 2005 Daylight Saving Time was shifted to begin on the second Sunday of March and end on the first Sunday of November.  A Department of Energy study found the extra daylight saves around 0.5% in total electricity daily in the US, equaling energy savings of 1.3 billion kilowatt-hours annually.

Next year, Daylight saving time will begin on Sunday, March 14th.
